title: NIST's approximate list pairs water's freeze with 32 Fahrenheit and its boil with 212
summary: On NIST's approximate touchstone list, the freezing point of water is 32 degrees Fahrenheit and the boiling point is 212 degrees Fahrenheit.
body: NIST's temperature page prints a table titled Touchstone Temperatures and labels the whole table approximate. In that table the freezing point of water is 32 degrees Fahrenheit and the boiling point of water is 212 degrees Fahrenheit. The Celsius wording on the same page, including the word about for the boil, already has its own card, so those Celsius figures are not rewritten here. This card is the Fahrenheit pair on the approximate list. It is not a new laboratory measurement, and a pressure other than the one assumed for the list is outside the page.

sources.title: SI Units – Temperature
sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.note: NIST SI temperature page, U.S. government work, public domain. No review date was printed on the page opened 2026-11-26. Supports the approximate touchstone rows that pair the freezing point of water with 32 degrees Fahrenheit and the boiling point with 212 degrees Fahrenheit. Celsius prose is not repeated.
